channel.title: Sunward
channel.description: Only good news. Each morning Sunward reads real newsrooms, keeps the stories where something got better, and says why in one line.

item.title: Two of the ‘Last Wild Ecosystems’ Untouched by Humans Are Declared New Sanctuaries
item.description: Two remote Pacific atolls, among the last ecosystems untouched by people, are now protected as sanctuaries. Evidence: Now policy. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Vitamin C could help block cancer-linked chemicals in your stomach, study finds
item.description: A model suggests vitamin C may stop cancer-linked chemicals forming in the stomach after nitrate-rich food. Evidence: Early research. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: A simple supplement could help your immune system fight cancer and viral infections
item.description: Researchers found a common amino acid, arginine, helps immune cells fight tumours and viruses in early tests. Evidence: Early research. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Looking for an ancient tree worth a detour? There’s an app for that
item.description: A Dutch designer built an app that maps great old trees around the world so others can visit them. How you can help: Look up the oldest tree near you and pay it a visit. Source: The Guardian Environment.

item.title: Dinosaurs may have been eating seaweed 100 million years ago
item.description: Chemical traces in fossil teeth suggest some dinosaurs ate seaweed over 100 million years ago. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Euclid discovers ancient cosmic beacons from the dawn of time, shining like a trillion suns
item.description: The Euclid telescope found 31 ancient quasars, two of them the brightest known from the early Universe. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: SpaceX successfully catches top of huge Starship rocket for first time
item.description: SpaceX caught the upper stage of its Starship rocket in mid-air for the first time, a step toward full reuse. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: BBC Science & Environment.

item.title: Couple with Autism and ADHD Find Passion Cleaning Filthy Street Signs
item.description: A married couple spend their free time scrubbing grimy street signs clean, and plan to keep going town by town. How you can help: Wipe down a grimy sign or pick up litter on your own street. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Indigenous students retrace Lewis and Clark’s historic journey: ‘We can’t protect what we cannot see’
item.description: Indigenous students are surveying wildlife along the Lewis and Clark route, two centuries on. How you can help: Log the wildlife you see on a citizen science app; surveys rely on many observers. Source: The Guardian Environment.

item.title: A giant icy world hiding beyond Pluto could be our sixth dwarf planet
item.description: Astronomers found a large icy body beyond Pluto that may become the sixth recognised dwarf planet. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Dr. King’s Lost Draft of ‘I Have a Dream’ Emerges from a Desk Drawer
item.description: A handwritten draft of the "I Have a Dream" speech has resurfaced from a desk drawer after six decades. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Man Rescues Trapped Neighbors from ‘Biblical’ Florida Flooding
item.description: A man waded through Florida floodwater to bring out two neighbours who could not leave on their own. How you can help: Check on neighbours who are ill or live alone when severe weather is forecast. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Infant Goes from 110 Seizures a Day to Seizure-Free with Experimental Treatment
item.description: A baby who had about 110 seizures a day became seizure-free after an experimental drug. Evidence: Early research. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Maui Is Becoming a Living Laboratory for Regenerative Tourism
item.description: After the 2023 fires, Maui is testing tourism that puts visitors to work restoring land and culture. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: When you travel, book locally owned stays and join a volunteer day where hosts offer one. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: National Trust takes back land for nature restoration
item.description: The National Trust is taking land back in hand to restore it, create wildlife habitat and open green space. How you can help: Volunteer for a habitat restoration day with a land charity near you. Source: BBC Science & Environment.

item.title: How two Princeton graduates built the world’s first microplastics removal system
item.description: Two graduates built a system that removes microplastics at wastewater plants before the water is released. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: Use a microfibre-catching laundry bag or filter to cut plastic fibres from your wash. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: China Switches on World’s Biggest Example of New, Cheap Green Energy Storage
item.description: The largest liquid-air energy storage plant yet is running, storing renewable power cheaply for later use. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: 100-Year-Old ‘Store Mom’ Surprised With Her First Birthday Party
item.description: Staff at the shop where a 100-year-old takes her daily walk threw her the first birthday party of her life. How you can help: Say hello to the regulars you see each day; small routines matter to people living alone. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: ‘There’s a Georgia O’Keeffe in the Closet’ – Words that Led to Painting’s Joyous Rediscovery
item.description: A Georgia O'Keeffe painting turned up in a family closet during a clear-out and is back in view. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Brave Teens Execute Paddleboard Rescue of Flooded Neighbors – ‘Faith in Humanity Restored’
item.description: Teenagers paddled out on boards to bring a mother and her son to safety when emergency crews could not reach them. How you can help: Learn your neighbours' names; in an emergency they are often the first help to arrive. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Crows can make decisions twice as fast as humans, scientists discover
item.description: Crows make visual decisions in 235 milliseconds, about twice as fast as people, a study found. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: AI-powered bionic eye breakthrough could help the blind see again
item.description: An AI model now predicts what a blind man sees through his brain implant, making bionic vision more precise. Evidence: Early research. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: A butterfly that fooled scientists for 200 years finally reveals its secrets
item.description: A well-known tropical butterfly turned out to be three species, one new to science. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Earth's fiery birth may have created hundreds of oceans' worth of water
item.description: Experiments suggest Earth made its own water as hot rock reacted with hydrogen in its early atmosphere. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Imagining the Mossy Cities of the Future
item.description: Designers in Germany are developing moss panels that cool and clean city air where trees cannot grow. Evidence: Early research. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: After a decade of community pressure, LA bans oil drilling for good
item.description: After a decade of pressure from residents, Los Angeles has banned oil drilling within the city. Evidence: Now policy. How you can help: Attend a local council meeting; steady neighbourhood pressure is what moved this decision. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: For Centuries, Visitors Walked Right by 280 Unseen Ice Age Cave Paintings
item.description: About 280 Ice Age engravings were found in a Spanish cave that visitors had walked past for centuries. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Brown Bear Population in Spain Doubles With Incredible Increase of its Breeding Range
item.description: Cantabrian brown bears have doubled to about 370 in twenty years and now roam 6,500 square miles. Evidence: Proven at scale. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: ‘I pulled him out, I heard more screaming’ – How a Cadet Saved a Father and Son from Drowning
item.description: A merchant marine cadet pulled a father and his adult son from a pool and both survived. How you can help: Take a CPR and water-rescue class; a few hours of training can save a life. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Paralysis Could Not Stop Her: How This 84-year-old Made Good on Her Musical Promise
item.description: An 84-year-old who recovered from paralysis returned to her rehab home to play piano for the patients. How you can help: Ask a local care home whether it welcomes volunteer musicians or visitors. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: What We’re Reading: An 80-Cent Plastic Bag Is Saving Mothers’ Lives
item.description: An 80-cent plastic bag used at births is helping save mothers' lives. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: Scientists discover a giant 66-pound rodent that lived 34 million years ago
item.description: Fossils from Thailand reveal a 66-pound rodent that lived 34 million years ago. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: 237-million-year-old fossils reveal a bizarre armored sea amphibian
item.description: Fossils from China show an armoured amphibian lived in the sea 237 million years ago. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Prince Bashangezi turned personal loss into peer tutoring for refugee students
item.description: A young man who lost schooling in lockdown now runs peer tutoring for refugee students. How you can help: Offer an hour a week of tutoring through a local school or library. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: Brazil releases the world’s first fossil fuel phaseout roadmap
item.description: Brazil has published the first national roadmap for phasing out fossil fuels. Evidence: Now policy. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: Astronomers discover hidden alien planet in James Webb images
item.description: A new image-cleaning method uncovered a hidden planet in James Webb data and could reveal many more. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: ‘Nothing short of a miracle’ – Rescuers Find Boy with Autism Missing for 3 Days
item.description: A six-year-old boy missing for three days in Kentucky was found safe by a volunteer searcher. How you can help: Join a local volunteer search and rescue team; many train newcomers. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: A Viral Video Led Strangers to Raise $76,000 for a Full-Time Caregiver
item.description: Strangers who saw a doorbell video gave more than $76,000 to a woman who spends her days caring for others. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Paleontologists discover “one-in-a-million” fossil with 450-million-year-old soft tissue
item.description: A 450-million-year-old fossil of a starfish relative preserves its soft tissue in rare detail. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: NASA’s CHAPEA Mars crew finally emerges after more than a year in isolation
item.description: Four volunteers finished more than a year in a simulated Mars habitat, growing food and rationing supplies. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Electric ferries that fly above water are arriving in the US
item.description: Electric ferries that lift above the water on foils, using far less energy, are starting service in US cities. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: Colleges Are Getting Creative to Help Students With Kids
item.description: Rural colleges are adding play corners, childcare help and flexible advising so student parents can finish. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: In Alaska’s capital, food comes by water, air or, most often, community sharing
item.description: In Juneau, where little food can be grown, neighbours keep each other fed by sharing fish, game and harvests. How you can help: Share surplus garden produce or a catch with neighbours or a community fridge. Source: The Guardian Environment.

item.title: The Spark: When Communities Own the Land, Housing Stays Affordable
item.description: Community land trusts keep homes affordable by holding the land in shared ownership. Evidence: Proven at scale. How you can help: Look up whether your area has a community land trust and attend an open meeting. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: The Montana Ranch Where Autistic People Are Wranglers and Guides
item.description: At a Montana guest ranch, autistic adults work as wranglers, guides, cooks and concierges. Evidence: Proven at scale. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: ‘It’s all God’s creation’: farmers continue a ‘Jewishly inspired’ agrarian tradition
item.description: A growing number of Jewish Americans are finding purpose and community through small farms. Source: The Guardian Environment.

item.title: How to move 1,300 plants for Kew's Palm House mega makeover
item.description: Kew is moving 1,300 plants to safety so its historic Palm House can be restored. Source: BBC Science & Environment.
